About 
the Report
Our Approach to Reporting
At Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
(“Metropolis” or “the Company” or "MHL"), we continue to strengthen our commitment to high-quality, transparent, and stakeholder-centric corporate reporting. This Annual Report presents an integrated view of our performance and progress  for the financial year ended  March
 31, 2026 (FY 2025-26). It 
off
ers a comprehensive lens into 
our strategy, business model, governance, risks, and outcomes across financial and non-financial parameters, demonstrating how we continue to create sustainable value in an evolving healthcare landscape.
Basis of Reporting
For the FY 2025-26 reporting cycle, we have further enhanced the depth and relevance of our disclosures to reflect the needs of a diverse stakeholder base, shareholders, patients, partners, regulators, employees, and the communities we serve.
Our reporting approach is guided 
by the principles of connectivity, materiality, consistency, comparability, and strategic orientation, ensuring that stakeholders gain meaningful insights into our performance and future direction.
Frameworks and Guidelines
The contents of this report are aligned with leading global and Indian reporting frameworks. It has been prepared in accordance with:

Maximising Capabilities. 
Amplifying Growth.
For over four decades, 
Metropolis Healthcare has earned the trust of clinicians, hospitals and patients through scientific excellence, diagnostic accuracy and uncompromising quality. Every investment we have made in science, technology, digital capabilities, laboratory infrastructure and specialised diagnostics has been driven by a single belief: stronger capabilities create stronger outcomes.
FY26 was about unlocking 
the full potential of our capabilities – creating stronger momentum for sustainable growth and lasting value.
Building on the strong foundations established 
over the past few years, we shifted our focus from expanding capabilities to maximising the value they create. Guided by our Maxify philosophy of maximising capabilities to amplify sustainable growth, we focused on translating our investments into stronger execution, higher productivity and scalable growth, creating a resilient platform for long-term value creation.
At Metropolis, we believe growth is amplified 
when capabilities work together. Scientific excellence strengthens clinical confidence. Technology enhances productivity. Digital innovation improves customer experience. Operational discipline reinforces quality and consistency. Together, these capabilities create a business that is more agile, more resilient and better positioned to seize future opportunities while delivering value for patients, clinicians, partners and shareholders.FY26 marked an important 
milestone in our journey.
02Annual Report 2025-26
=== page 6 ===
Together, these strategic 
priorities strengthened the capabilities that differentiate Metropolis – creating a stronger, more resilient organisation equipped to accelerate sustainable growth and deliver long-term value for all stakeholders.
Building on the Maxify philosophy, 
FY26 was defined by focused execution across five strategic priorities. Together, these initiatives strengthened the way we operate, innovate and serve our stakeholders, creating the momentum that will power Metropolis' next phase of growth.Capability  
in ActionWe embedded quality across every stage of the diagnostic value 
chain through our integrated Quality Intelligence Framework. By standardising laboratory practices, strengthening governance and leveraging digital quality oversight, we enhanced diagnostic accuracy, consistency and compliance, reinforcing trust while building a resilient platform for sustainable growth.Embedding Quality Excellence
We embedded productivity as an organisation-wide discipline through workflow optimisation, scientific manpower planning, automation and process excellence. By improving resource utilisation and operational efficiency, we unlocked greater value from our existing network and capabilities.Driving Enterprise-wide Productivity
We deepened customer engagement by accelerating digital adoption, enriching the B2B experience and introducing lifecycle management across customer touchpoints. Together, these actions delivered more connected, responsive and seamless customer journeys.Advancing Customer-led Growth
We expanded our specialised diagnostics portfolio while advancing our genomics capabilities, reinforcing our leadership in high-value diagnostics and strengthening our readiness for the future of precision medicine.Strengthening Scientific Leadership
As acquisitions matured, we focussed on integration and value realisation. By capturing operational synergies, strengthening cross-functional collaboration and institutionalising best practices, we enhanced organisational agility and created a scalable platform for future growth.Building an Integrated Enterprise

TruHealth 
Maximising Prevention.  
Amplifying Lifelong Health.
Strengthening Leadership in Preventive Healthcare 
As healthcare increasingly shifts towards prevention and early risk 
identification, TruHealth is strengthening Metropolis' presence in the growing 
preventive healthcare segment through an integrated, patient-centric model. 
By combining advanced diagnostics, comprehensive health assessments and 
expert clinical guidance, TruHealth enables more informed health decisions 
while creating a differentiated preventive healthcare experience. This 
integrated approach continues to drive premiumisation, strengthen customer 
engagement and support long-term growth.

Specialty Diagnostics
Maximising Precision Diagnostics. 
Amplifying High-Value Growth.
Specialty Diagnostics has become one of Metropolis' key growth drivers, 
powered by a diversified portfolio of advanced diagnostics spanning Oncology, Chronic & Infectious Diseases, Gastroenterology, Neurology & Nephrology, and Women & Child Health. Combining cutting-edge technologies with deep scientific and clinical expertise, we deliver clinically actionable insights that strengthen clinician confidence, accelerate premiumisation and support sustainable long-term growth.
The integration of CORE Diagnostics has significantly strengthened our precision oncology capabilities, combining 
deep scientific expertise in molecular diagnostics and genomics with Metropolis' nationwide network and trusted clinician relationships.

Metropolis at a Glance
Maximising Science. Amplifying Trust.
Diagnostics trusted by doctors and patients alike.
Established in 1981, Metropolis 
Healthcare is one of India's leading diagnostic companies, serving millions of patients through a network built on clinical expertise, advanced laboratory infrastructure and a patient-first approach. Over the last seven years, we have delivered a 12% revenue CAGR, reflecting our consistent focus on quality, innovation and sustainable growth.Trust is the core of our business, and it begins with 
clinicians. Reinforced by rigorous quality systems, 99.99% report accuracy and CAP proficiency scores consistently above 99%, that trust is the foundation of every diagnostic insight we deliver. As healthcare becomes more data driven and personalised, we continue to strengthen our capabilities through technology, automation and digital innovation. AI enabled workflows and integrated laboratory systems are enhancing efficiency, accessibility and customer experience. Our leadership in specialty diagnostics, including molecular diagnostics, oncology and genomics, is reinforced through continued investment in scientific talent and strategic acquisitions that deepen our expertise in high growth markets.
Our Vision
To be a respected healthcare brand trusted by clinicians, patients and stakeholders. Positively impact the lives of patients in their most anxious times and turn their anxiety into assurance

Geographic Presence
Maximising Reach.  
Amplifying Access.
Strengthening access through a growing network of diagnostic excellence.
INDIA
In FY26, Metropolis 
expanded its reach while strengthening its scientific leadership across key markets. Our network crossed the milestone of 5,000+ service network touchpoints, serving over 750 towns across India through a scalable hub-and-spoke model that combines regional access with consistent quality standards.Strategic acquisitions and organic expansion strengthened our 
presence in high-growth regions, particularly North India, where revenue contribution increased to 17% of the business. The integration of Core Diagnostics (Delhi NCR), Scientific Pathology (Agra), Dr Ahujas' Pathology and Imaging Centre (DAPIC - Dehradun) and Ambika Pathology (Kolhapur) expanded our regional footprint while enhancing capabilities in oncology, genomics and specialty diagnostics. By combining scale, scientific expertise and operational excellence, we are making advanced diagnostics more accessible across India.

=== page 16 ===
AFRICA & INTERNATIONAL MARKETS:
Over the past decade, Metropolis has established a strong presence in five African countries through company-
managed laboratories and collection centres in Kenya, Zambia, Ghana, Tanzania and Uganda. In addition, we serve a diverse network of B2B partners across 16 international markets, including the UAE (Dubai and Abu Dhabi), Oman and Qatar in the Middle East; Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Uzbekistan and Vietnam in Asia; and Mauritius, Nigeria, Congo, Cameroon, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe in Africa.
Through our international network, we extend access to high-quality diagnostics while leveraging Metropolis’ 
scientific expertise, quality standards and specialised testing capabilities across diverse healthcare markets.

Letter from the Chairperson
Maximising What 
We Have Built. Amplifying What Lies Ahead.
Dear Shareholders,
Every year, I begin this letter by 
asking myself one simple question: Did we deliver on the commitments we made?
Not only in terms of financial 
performance, but in the way we strengthened our science, served our patients, supported clinicians, empowered our people and prepared Metropolis for the future.
Looking back at FY26, I can answer 
that question with confidence. Yes, we did.
FY26 was not defined by a single 
milestone. It was the culmination of years of deliberate investment in scientific capability, technology, operational excellence and talent.Delivering on Our Commitments
The year rewarded that patience. Group revenue grew 23.6% to `
 1,646 crore, EBITD
A rose 32% 
to ` 401 crore, and profit aft
er 
tax increased 31% to `  191 crore. 
Organic rev
enue growth of 13.7% 
exceeded the guidance of 12–13% we had provided at the start of the year, while organic margins recovered to pre-pandemic levels of around 26%. We also kept a promise on integration: within four quarters of acquisition, Core Diagnostics moved from an EBITDA margin of negative 2% to high single digits — exactly as committed within one year.Beyond the numbers, what encourages me most is how we grew. Higher patient volumes, a richer test mix and better productivity drove our growth, rather than price increases. To me, that is the healthiest kind of growth: earned from more patients choosing us and more clinicians prescribing deeper science, and delivered with disciplined capital. The investments of the past several years are no longer promises on a slide; they are showing up in our results.

For 45 years, Metropolis has earned

The Moment We Are In
The timing matters because India's 
healthcare landscape is undergoing a transformation that is both rapid and irreversible. Rising investment in health, progressive policy reforms and the accelerating adoption of digital infrastructure are reshaping how care is delivered and accessed across the country.
We are beginning to see the early 
contours of managed care emerge, with ambulatory care, primary care and hospitalisation being integrated within a single city. This evolution is taking different forms across India, with hospital-led models in some markets and primary care-led models in others. While it remains, uncertain which model will prevail, diagnostics sits at the centre of every patient journey, regardless of where care begins.The shift is equally evident in the evolution of healthcare delivery models. App-first platforms have proved effective at acquiring customers, yet profitability has often remained elusive. As a result, several are now investing in physical healthcare infrastructure while continuing to expand their digital presence. This reinforces a belief we have long held: technology should extend the reach of trusted physical infrastructure, not replace it.
Against this backdrop, diagnostics 
has assumed an even more critical role. A diagnosis is not simply a test result; it is the starting point

Dear Shareholders,
Trust is the moat this company 
is built on. My letter is about the machinery that renews it every day. It is about the network we have built, the science we operationalise, the productivity we are engineering into our operating model, and the discipline with which we integrate what we acquire.
FY26 was the year the Metropolis 
3.0 strategy moved from investment to evidence. Over three years, we expanded the network, upgraded laboratory infrastructure, accelerated digital adoption and completed four acquisitions. This year, that build-out began to show what it can do.
An Asset-Light Network, By 
Design
Today, Metropolis serves more than 
750 towns through 5,000+ service touchpoints and 210+ clinical laboratories. Just as important as the size of this network is its architecture. Our hub and spoke model, with a Global Reference Laboratory at the apex supported by regional reference laboratories, satellite units and an expanding network of collection centres, provides a scalable foundation for growth. With our four-year network expansion programme now complete, we are entering a more asset-light phase. New collection centres, primarily franchise-led, are increasing volumes across our existing laboratory network, improving capacity utilisation without requiring proportionate capital investment. Simultaneously, expanding specialty testing capabilities at regional reference laboratories is bringing advanced diagnostics closer to patients and reducing turnaround times across our markets.
Where the Growth Came From
FY26 demonstrated the strength of our operating model and our ability to translate strategic priorities into disciplined execution. Higher productivity, an improving business mix, stronger revenue per patient and healthy patient volume growth reflected the quality and consistency of our execution.
Growth remained well balanced 
across both B2C and B2B segments, reinforcing the resilience of our business model. Within B2B, we continued to enhance the quality of our portfolio by reducing our dependence on low-margin institutional business while deepening long-term partnerships with hospitals, corporates, pharmaceutical companies and clinical research organisations. Investments in digital partner platforms further simplified engagement and strengthened service delivery.
Preventive healthcare continued to 
gain momentum through TruHealth. During the year, we expanded

Genomics: Building the 
Next Frontier of Specialty Diagnostics
The Metropolis Centre of 
Genomics represents a significant milestone in our journey towards advancing precision diagnostics and personalised healthcare. Established as an integrated genomics platform, the Centre brings together advanced molecular diagnostics, next-generation sequencing (NGS), bioinformatics, clinical interpretation, and genetic counselling capabilities to deliver clinically actionable insights across oncology, reproductive health, neurology, rare diseases, infectious diseases, and preventive genomics.
Built on the combined strengths 
of Metropolis’ Global Reference Laboratory in Mumbai and Core Diagnostics’ specialised genomics laboratory in Delhi NCR, the platform operates through two CAP-accredited national referral laboratories. It is supported by multidisciplinary teams of molecular pathologists, genomic scientists, bioinformaticians, and certified genetic counsellors.  By integrating advanced genomic science with patient 
care pathways, it enables precise 
diagnosis, therapy selection, disease risk assessment and long-term disease management.
During FY
 2025-26, the C
entre 
further strengthened its capabilities 
through investments in advanced sequencing technologies, expansion of its genomics portfolio, enhancement of bioinformatics and clinical interpretation expertise, and integration of AI-assisted reporting within genomic workflows. It also expanded its scientific ecosystem through collaborations with leading academic and healthcare institutions, including AIIMS New Delhi, supporting translational research and accelerating the adoption of genomic medicine in India.
The Centre of Genomics launch at Core Metropolis, Gurugram, Delhi NCR, India
With a vision to create one of India's most comprehensive and 
integrated genomic diagnostic platforms, the Centre of Genomics continues to drive scientific innovation and advance precision healthcare. We combine advanced technologies, multidisciplinary expertise and research-led collaboration to strengthen our ability to deliver high-quality genomic insights, improve patient outcomes and build a strong foundation for the future of personalised medicine.

Beyond Work, Together
A strong culture is built not only through the work we do, but through the experiences we share. Across regions, 
our teams came together to celebrate festivals, participate in sporting events, recognise achievements and connect through town halls and team celebrations. These moments reflect the diversity, camaraderie and shared purpose that define life at Metropolis, creating an environment where people feel connected, valued and inspired.Successful acquisitions are measured not only by financial outcomes but by how effectively people, culture and capabilities come together. FY26 marked a landmark year for Metropolis with the integration of four acquisitions, the highest number integrated in a single year in the Company's journey. Our people-first integration approach ensured that this transformation was not only operationally seamless but also culturally successful. Our approach began with understanding each acquired organisation's culture, strengths and ways of working before thoughtfully aligning them with the Metropolis ecosystem.
The integration journey began with building trust 
through transparent communication, leadership townhalls, regular market visits and continuous employee engagement. We provided clarity on what would change, what would remain unchanged, and the opportunities that lay ahead, enabling employees to Mergers & Acquisitions: Integrating People. Preserving Strengths.
navigate the transition with confidence. Critical talent was identified early, with focussed efforts to retain key capabilities, preserve institutional knowledge, enhance visibility with business leaders across Metropolis, and create meaningful career pathways within the organisation.
Alongside aligning people policies, systems and 
payroll processes, acquired teams were progressively integrated into planning, performance and people practices, ensuring a consistent employee experience while preserving the strengths that had made each organisation successful. By the end of the integration journey, they were no longer operating as separate entities but as Metropolis, united by a shared purpose, aligned ways of working and a collective commitment to delivering excellence and sustainable growth.

MedEngage
Advancing Equity in Medical Education
Launched in 2018, MedEngage is Metropolis Healthcare's 
flagship initiative dedicated to expanding access to medical education and research opportunities for deserving students and young researchers. We provide scholarships, research grants, mentorship and experiential learning opportunities to equip aspiring healthcare professionals with the knowledge, skills and exposure needed to contribute to India's evolving healthcare ecosystem.
We remain committed to socio-economic inclusion by 
reducing barriers to medical education for talented students from underserved and aspirational districts. We combine financial assistance with research exposure, industry engagement and mentorship to foster innovation, leadership and professional growth among emerging healthcare professionals.

GLOBAL ECONOMY 
Global economic growth remained stable but moderate, 
with global GDP projected at 3.4% in 2025, moderating to 3.1% in 2026 before recovering slightly to 3.2% in 2027, reflecting a steady but subdued expansion. The global outlook continues to be shaped by persistent geopolitical tensions, evolving trade dynamics, and uneven regional growth patterns.
Ongoing conflicts, including the Russia–Ukraine war 
and instability in the Middle East, remain key sources of uncertainty. These developments are exerting pressure on energy markets, disrupting supply chains, and contributing to volatility in global financial conditions. Trade fragmentation and geopolitical disruptions have also affected critical commodity flows and key shipping routes, resulting in pricing pressures and tighter financial conditions, particularly across Asia.
Inflationary pressures are gradually easing, with global 
inflation projected to decline from approximately 4.1% in 2025 to 3.8% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, although the pace of moderation remains uneven across regions. Energy price volatility and geopolitical developments continue to pose upside risks to inflation, requiring central banks to maintain a cautious and balanced policy stance.
Growth trends vary across regions. Advanced economies 
are expected to grow modestly at 1.7%–1.9%, with the United States demonstrating relative resilience, while the Euro Area and Japan continue to face subdued economic momentum. In contrast, Emerging Markets and Developing Economies are projected to grow at just above 4%, supported by domestic consumption and infrastructure investment, although elevated debt levels and tighter financial conditions remain key risks.
Regionally, the Middle East continues to demonstrate 
resilience, supported by strong domestic demand, while Southeast Asia remains an important growth driver, albeit with moderating momentum in certain economies following strong performance in the previous year.

INDIAN ECONOMY 
India’s macroeconomic environment in FY 2025-26 remained resilient, supported by strong domestic demand, sustained public investment, and stable macroeconomic fundamentals. Real GDP growth is estimated at approximately 7.4% in FY 2025-26 , reflecting continued momentum across key sectors, including services, manufacturing, and construction. Favourable monsoon conditions supported agricultural output and rural demand, contributing to overall economic stability.
Inflationary pressures moderated during the year, 
supported by easing food prices and effective policy measures.
Consumption trends remained mixed. While urban 
consumption showed some moderation due to elevated food prices and housing costs, underlying demand remained stable, supported by income growth and improving rural consumption. Private consumption continued to be a key growth driver, reflecting resilience in domestic demand.
Policy support remained strong, with continued focus 
on infrastructure development, manufacturing, and formalisation of the economy. Government initiatives aimed at improving ease of doing business, enhancing digital infrastructure, and expanding financial inclusion are supporting long-term economic growth.

Looking ahead, India’s real GDP growth is projected at 
approximately 6.4% for FY 2026-27, with upside potential as credit growth strengthens, investment activity accelerates, and structural reforms continue to deepen. INDIAN HEAL THCARE INDUSTRY
India’s healthcare sector continued to demonstrate resilient growth in FY 2025-26, supported by rising demand for specialised healthcare services, steady capacity expansion by hospital chains, and increasing formalisation across segments, including diagnostics. The sector has expanded significantly in both scale and scope over the past decade, driven by rising public and private investments, wider insurance coverage, and improving service delivery standards.
India continues to benefit from a large pool of highly 
qualified medical professionals and a strong cost advantage, positioning it as a competitive healthcare destination globally. However, structural challenges persist, particularly in the form of infrastructure imbalances across regions. A significant proportion of healthcare infrastructure remains concentrated in urban areas, with approximately 65–70% of hospital beds located in cities, while nearly 65% of the population resides in rural regions. This disparity underscores a substantial opportunity for both public and private sector investments aimed at expanding healthcare access in underserved markets.
The sector continues to attract investor interest, with 
private equity investments in Indian healthcare remaining robust, reflecting long-term confidence in the sector’s growth potential. At the same time, policy support remains a key driver of expansion. The Union Budget FY 2026-27 introduced several measures aimed at strengthening the healthcare ecosystem, including an allocation of approximately `10,000 crore towards the Biopharma 
SHAKTI initiative, focussed on advancing research, innovation, and domestic capabilities in pharmaceuticals and life sciences.
Further, the estimated healthcare expenditure for FY 2026-
27 is projected at approximately `1,04,599 crore, reflecting

DIAGNOSTICS INDUSTRY
The Indian diagnostics industry continues to be one of the fastest-growing segments within the broader healthcare ecosystem, supported by increasing health awareness, rising disease burden, and improving access to diagnostic services. The market was estimated at approximately USD 10.9–11.0 billion in 2025, reflecting steady expansion driven by rising patient volumes and increasing test penetration.
The industry remains highly fragmented, with over 1.3 lakh 
laboratories across the country, dominated by standalone laboratories and hospital-based diagnostic centres. Standalone laboratories account for approximately 40–42% of the market, supported by their extensive geographic reach and accessibility. However, the industry is witnessing a gradual shift towards organised diagnostic chains, driven by increasing consumer preference for quality, accuracy, and reliability, as well as the need for scalable and technology-enabled operations.
This transition towards organised players has accelerated 
in recent years, with the share of organised chains increasing from approximately 15% in FY20 to over 22% in FY24, supported by consolidation, network expansion, and technology adoption. The trend is further reinforced by increasing merger and acquisition activity and the growing presence of national and regional chains.
From a service mix perspective, pathology continues 
to dominate the diagnostics landscape, accounting for approximately 65% of the total market, driven by its routine use in disease diagnosis, preventive health check-ups, and chronic disease management. Radiology constitutes the remaining 35%, including imaging modalities such as X-ray, ultrasound, CT scan, MRI, PET-CT, and nuclear imaging.
The industry continues to be largely physician-led, with 
approximately 45–50% of diagnostic volumes originating from clinician referrals, reflecting the central role of diagnostics in clinical decision-making. At the same time, direct-to-consumer engagement is increasing, supported by rising health awareness, digital platforms, and the growing adoption of preventive healthcare.
Geographically, the diagnostics market remains 
concentrated in urban centres, which account for approximately 70–75% of total revenues, supported by better healthcare infrastructure, higher awareness, and stronger purchasing power. However, this concentration also highlights a significant opportunity for expansion in Tier II, Tier III, and rural markets. While nearly 70% of India’s population resides in rural areas, it contributes only ~24% of the diagnostics market, indicating substantial headroom for future growth.
Regionally, North India continues to lead the diagnostics 
market with a share of approximately 28–32%, followed by South and West India, while East India remains relatively underpenetrated but is expected to witness faster growth driven by improving infrastructure and increasing healthcare access.

The industry has transitioned into a more stable, volume-
driven growth phase post the COVID-19 period. Revenue growth is now supported by steady increases in patient volumes, expansion into Tier II and Tier III cities, and improving realisations. A key structural trend shaping the industry is the rapid growth of preventive and wellness testing, with its share increasing from approximately 8% in FY18 to ~11% in FY24, and expected to reach ~15% by FY28, reflecting a shift towards proactive health management.

INDUSTRY OUTLOOK
The outlook for the Indian diagnostics industry remains strong, supported by favourable demographics, increasing health awareness, rising adoption of preventive healthcare, expanding healthcare infrastructure and continued formalisation of the sector. These structural trends, together with improving healthcare accessibility and increasing investments across the healthcare ecosystem, are expected to sustain long-term demand for diagnostic services. 
The industry is projected to grow at a CAGR of 
approximately 11–12% over the medium term, with the market expected to reach USD 15–16 billion over the next five years and further expand to approximately USD 28–29 billion by 2034. Growth will continue to be driven by the rising prevalence of non-communicable diseases, including diabetes, cardiovascular disorders and cancer, increasing health insurance penetration, and growing consumer preference for preventive healthcare and early disease detection. The Indian diagnostics market is also witnessing a gradual shift towards organised diagnostic providers. Expansion into Tier II, Tier III and rural markets, supported by improving healthcare infrastructure, increasing affordability and greater accessibility, is expected to create significant growth opportunities. Organised players are well positioned to benefit from these trends by leveraging trusted brands, quality standards, scalable operating models and wider geographic reach.
Technology will continue to serve as a key enabler of 
industry transformation, enhancing diagnostic accuracy, operational efficiency and patient experience. Continued adoption of automation, digital platforms and advanced diagnostic technologies is expected to improve accessibility, reduce turnaround times and support scalable growth across the diagnostics value chain.
While pricing pressures in routine diagnostics, evolving 
regulatory requirements and competitive intensity may continue to influence the operating environment, the industry’s long-term fundamentals remain robust. The continued shift towards organised, quality-driven and technology-enabled diagnostics providers is expected to support sustainable growth and long-term value creation.

GOVERNMENT INITIATIVES DRIVING DIAGNOSTICS 
INDUSTRY GROWTH
As diseases increasingly cross borders and health 
awareness grows worldwide, the sector is emerging as a critical piece of the country’s healthcare story. The Indian diagnostic industry is growing due to regulatory actions by the Government of India. A series of policies are launched to aid the sector and enhance its accessibility and affordability. These shifts are gradually but meaningfully reshaping how the diagnostics sector operates - and for organised players, which spells a significant long-term opportunity.
Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya 
Yojana (PM-JAY)
The Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana 
(PM-JAY), introduced in 2018, continues to be a cornerstone of India’s healthcare reform agenda, providing health insurance coverage of up to ` 5 lakh per family for secondary 
and tertiary care hospitalisation. The scheme has significantly expanded access to healthcare services for economically vulnerable populations, leading to increased healthcare utilisation and earlier disease detection. The recent extension of coverage to senior citizens above the age of 70 further enhances the inclusivity and reach of the programme. The expansion of insurance coverage has also contributed to higher diagnostic volumes, as hospital-based care pathways increasingly incorporate structured testing and screening protocols.
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Health and Wellness 
Centres)
The government has made substantial progress in 
strengthening primary healthcare infrastructure through the expansion of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, formerly known as Health and Wellness Centres. With over 1.78 lakh centres operational across the country, these facilities provide preventive, promotive, and basic diagnostic services at the grassroots level. The focus on early screening, particularly for non-communicable diseases, is enabling timely diagnosis and referral, thereby increasing demand for diagnostic services. This shift towards preventive care is expected to play a critical role in improving long-term health outcomes while driving sustained growth in diagnostic testing.
84
Annual Report 2025-26
=== page 88 ===
Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)
The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is driving the 
development of a unified digital health ecosystem in India. Through the creation of interoperable electronic health records and digital health identities, the initiative is enabling seamless data exchange across healthcare providers. With over 79 crore ABHA IDs generated and more than 65 crore health records linked, ABDM is improving continuity of care and enabling data-driven clinical decision-making. The digital integration of healthcare systems is also enhancing diagnostic accuracy, streamlining reporting processes, and improving overall patient experience.
e-Sanjeevani Telemedicine Platform
The government’s e-Sanjeevani platform has emerged as a key enabler of telemedicine adoption in India, significantly improving healthcare access in remote and underserved regions. With over 37 crore consultations conducted through a hub-and-spoke model, the platform connects primary healthcare centres with specialists across the country. This expansion of telemedicine is increasingly integrating diagnostics into remote care pathways, particularly for follow-up testing, chronic disease monitoring, and specialist consultations.
PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission 
(PM-ABHIM)
The PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission 
(PM-ABHIM), with an outlay of approximately `64,000 
crore, aims to strengthen healthcare infrastructure across primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. The initiative focusses on enhancing diagnostic capacity, building critical care infrastructure, and improving preparedness for future public health emergencies. These investments are expected to improve healthcare access and strengthen the overall resilience of the healthcare ecosystem.
Free Diagnostics Services Initiative (FDSI)
The Free Diagnostics Services Initiative under the National Health Mission is aimed at improving affordability and accessibility of diagnostic services by providing essential tests at public health facilities. This initiative helps reduce out-of-pocket expenditure for patients while simultaneously increasing testing volumes and strengthening diagnostic infrastructure across government healthcare systems.
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for 
Medical Devices
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Medical 
Devices is designed to promote domestic manufacturing of high-value medical equipment, including diagnostic imaging devices such as CT scanners and MRI systems. By reducing dependence on imports and encouraging local production, the scheme is expected to improve accessibility and affordability of advanced diagnostic technologies, while strengthening India’s position as a manufacturing hub for medical devices.
Biopharma SHAKTI Initiative
The Biopharma SHAKTI initiative represents a significant step towards strengthening India’s capabilities in pharmaceutical research, biotechnology, and advanced diagnostics. With a proposed allocation of approximately `10,000 crore, the initiative aims to promote innovation, expand clinical trial infrastructure, and support the development of next-generation healthcare solutions. These efforts are aligned with broader industry trends, including increasing investments in high-value diagnostic segments such as genomics and oncology.

COMPANY OVERVIEW
Metropolis Healthcare Limited (“Metropolis” or “the 
Company”) is one of India’s leading and most trusted pathology laboratory chains, with over four decades of scientific excellence and a strong reputation for delivering accurate, reliable and high-quality diagnostic services. Established in 1981, the Company has built enduring trust among clinicians, patients and healthcare institutions through its unwavering commitment to quality, innovation and patient-centric care.
The Company operates a comprehensive diagnostics 
network across India and select international markets, supported by 210+ clinical laboratories, a 5,000+ service network, and a presence across 750+ towns in 28 States and 7 Union Territories. Its scalable hub-and-spoke operating model enables efficient sample logistics, faster turnaround times and consistent quality, while expanding access to advanced diagnostic services across diverse geographies. Internationally, Metropolis has established a strong presence across Africa through company-managed laboratories and collection centres in 5 African countries including Kenya, Zambia, Ghana, Tanzania and Uganda. In addition, the Company serve a diverse network of B2B partners across 16 international markets, including the UAE (Dubai and Abu Dhabi), Oman and Qatar in the Middle East; Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Uzbekistan and Vietnam in Asia; and Mauritius, Nigeria, Congo, Cameroon, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe in Africa.Management Discussion and Analysis (Contd.)

EMERGING TRENDS IN DIAGNOSTIC INDUSTRY
Digital and AI-Driven Diagnostics
Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced analytics and digital 
technologies are transforming diagnostic workflows by improving analytical accuracy, reducing turnaround times and enabling predictive insights. The increasing adoption of intelligent automation, AI-assisted diagnostics and connected digital platforms is strengthening data-driven clinical decision-making across pathology, radiology and genomics. Metropolis continues to invest in AI-assisted diagnostic workflows, digital platforms and intelligent automation to enhance operational efficiency, strengthen scientific capabilities and deliver more accurate, technology-enabled diagnostics.
Rising Adoption of Preventive and Wellness Testing
Growing health awareness, increasing lifestyle-related diseases and rising consumer focus on early detection are accelerating demand for preventive healthcare and routine wellness testing. Wellness diagnostics continue to outpace the broader diagnostics market, supported by corporate wellness programmes, digital health adoption and expanding insurance coverage. Metropolis is strengthening its preventive healthcare ecosystem through TruHealth, personalised wellness offerings, AI-enabled health insights and expanding digital and home-based service capabilities to improve accessibility and customer engagement.
Growth of Specialised and High-Value Diagnostics
The increasing prevalence of chronic diseases and the growing adoption of precision medicine are driving demand for specialised diagnostics, including molecular diagnostics, genomics and oncology testing. These high-value segments continue to improve the industry’s clinical relevance and revenue mix. Metropolis is expanding its specialised diagnostics portfolio through the Centre of Genomics, advanced molecular diagnostics, next-generation sequencing (NGS) and continuous investment in scientific innovation to strengthen its leadership in precision diagnostics.Acceleration of Point-of-Care and Home-Based 
Diagnostics
Consumer preference for convenient and technology-
enabled healthcare continues to drive demand for home sample collection, digital engagement and connected diagnostic services. Digital health solutions are improving accessibility while enabling more seamless patient experiences. Metropolis continues to strengthen its omnichannel service model through enhanced home collection services, digital platforms, mobile applications and technology-enabled customer journeys, improving convenience, accessibility and service responsiveness.
Personalised and Preventive Diagnostics: Shift 
towards Proactive Healthcare
Healthcare is increasingly shifting from reactive treatment 
to proactive prevention, with growing consumer demand for genetic testing, early cancer screening, wellness panels, and chronic disease risk profiling. AI-enabled analytics and longitudinal health data are supporting predictive risk assessment, enabling more informed clinical decision-making and improved patient outcomes. The Company continues to strengthen its capabilities in personalised and preventive diagnostics, including initiatives to enhance early detection and expand access to screening solutions. 
Industry Consolidation and Strategic Ecosystem 
Integration
The diagnostics sector in India continues to consolidate, 
with organised players gaining share from fragmented local laboratories. Larger chains are acquiring regional players to build scale, expand geographic reach, and standardise quality. In parallel, partnerships across health-tech, pharmaceutical, and public health ecosystems are enabling more integrated healthcare delivery models. The Company is aligned with this trend through selective acquisitions and collaborations aimed at strengthening its network and service capabilities.
Regulatory Focus and Quality Standardisation
Increasing regulatory oversight and greater emphasis on accreditation, quality assurance and laboratory standardisation are raising industry benchmarks and reinforcing the importance of scientific credibility. Metropolis continues to strengthen its quality ecosystem through NABL-accredited laboratories, internationally recognised quality standards, digital quality monitoring and robust governance practices, reinforcing trust, consistency and diagnostic excellence across its network.Management Discussion and Analysis (Contd.)

MAJOR GROWTH DRIVERS AND OPPORTUNITIES
Rising Burden of Lifestyle and Chronic Diseases
India is witnessing a sustained increase in non-
communicable diseases (NCDs), including cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, cancer and respiratory disorders, driving higher demand for specialised diagnostics, chronic disease monitoring and early detection. The increasing need for timely diagnosis is expanding the role of organised diagnostic providers. Metropolis is well positioned to capitalise on this trend through its comprehensive test portfolio, specialised diagnostics capabilities and expanding preventive healthcare offerings, enabling early diagnosis and improved disease management.
Demographic Shifts and Ageing Population
India’s ageing population is expected to drive increasing demand for preventive health assessments, chronic disease management and age-related diagnostics. Longer life expectancy and rising healthcare awareness are creating sustained demand for regular monitoring and personalised care. Metropolis is strengthening its preventive healthcare ecosystem, specialised diagnostics and wellness solutions to address the evolving healthcare needs of an ageing population.
Expansion in Tier II and Tier III Markets
Tier II and Tier III cities continue to emerge as significant growth markets, supported by improving healthcare infrastructure, rising incomes and increasing awareness of quality diagnostics. Organised diagnostic players are expected to benefit from expanding access and increasing formalisation of the sector. Metropolis continues to deepen its presence across these markets through network expansion, hub-and-spoke infrastructure and technology-enabled service delivery, improving accessibility while supporting sustainable long-term growth.
Increasing Health Insurance Penetration
The expansion of health insurance coverage through government schemes and private insurers is improving affordability and encouraging greater utilisation of diagnostic services. As financial barriers reduce, preventive and routine diagnostic testing is expected to witness stronger adoption. Metropolis is well positioned to benefit from this trend through its diversified service offerings, institutional partnerships and growing preventive healthcare portfolio.
Rising Income Levels and Health Awareness
Higher disposable incomes, increasing health awareness and changing consumer behaviour are accelerating demand for preventive healthcare and wellness diagnostics. Consumers are increasingly seeking routine health assessments, personalised health insights and early disease detection. Metropolis continues to strengthen its consumer-centric healthcare offerings through TruHealth, digital engagement platforms and personalised wellness solutions, supporting higher customer engagement and long-term growth.
Government Support and Policy Initiatives
Government initiatives focussed on expanding healthcare infrastructure, strengthening digital health ecosystems and improving healthcare accessibility continue to create favourable long-term opportunities for the diagnostics industry. Programmes such as Ayushman Bharat and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) are expected to improve access to organised diagnostic services. Metropolis continues to align its technology, quality systems and digital infrastructure with evolving healthcare priorities while expanding access to quality diagnostics across the country. 
Growth of Preventive Healthcare and Wellness 
Testing
Preventive healthcare and wellness diagnostics 
continue to be among the fastest-growing segments of the diagnostics industry, driven by increasing health consciousness, corporate wellness programmes and demand for early disease detection. This shift towards proactive healthcare is expected to support sustained growth in routine diagnostic testing. Metropolis continues to strengthen its preventive healthcare portfolio through TruHealth, integrated wellness solutions and personalised health programmes, enabling consumers to take a more proactive approach towards health management.
Global Opportunity for Indian Diagnostics Players
India’s scientific expertise, cost competitiveness and improving quality standards are creating opportunities for organised diagnostic companies to participate in the global diagnostics value chain. Growing acceptance of Indian laboratories and increasing demand for specialised testing present attractive long-term opportunities. Metropolis continues to strengthen its scientific capabilities, quality systems and advanced diagnostics infrastructure, positioning the Company to participate in emerging opportunities across specialised and international diagnostics.
THREATS
Workforce Shortage and Skill Gaps
The diagnostics industry continues to face a shortage of 
skilled professionals, including pathologists, radiologists, lab technicians, and phlebotomists. This challenge is more Management Discussion and Analysis (Contd.)
88
Annual Report 2025-26

pronounced in rural and semi-urban regions, where access 
to trained talent remains limited, potentially impacting service quality and expansion. Increasing regulatory requirements for accredited laboratories to employ qualified personnel, along with the need for continuous upskilling amid technological advancements, further add to talent-related pressures.
Competitive Intensity and Pricing Dynamics
The diagnostics industry continues to witness increasing competition from organised chains, hospital-based laboratories, and new entrants including digital health platforms and pharmaceutical companies. While pricing discipline has improved in recent years, competitive intensity may impact test realisations and volume growth, particularly in routine diagnostics, thereby exerting pressure on margins.
High Capital Expenditure and Operational Costs
Sustaining competitiveness requires ongoing investment in advanced diagnostic technologies, including molecular diagnostics and high-end imaging systems. These investments involve significant capital expenditure, along with recurring maintenance and infrastructure costs. The need for specialised personnel to operate such technologies further adds to operational expenses, which may impact profitability, particularly for smaller and mid-sized players.
Supply Chain Dependence and Import Exposure
The diagnostics sector remains dependent on imports for a significant proportion of reagents, consumables, Management Discussion and Analysis (Contd.)
and high-value medical equipment. This reliance exposes the industry to global supply chain disruptions, currency volatility, and geopolitical risks, which may lead to cost pressures and potential supply constraints.
Digital Transformation and Data Security Risks
While digitalisation is enhancing efficiency and access, it also introduces challenges related to infrastructure gaps and data security. The digital divide between urban and rural areas may limit the reach of technology-enabled services. Additionally, increasing digitisation of patient data heightens cybersecurity and data privacy risks, necessitating continued investment in secure systems and compliance frameworks.
Regulatory Complexity and Compliance Challenges
The regulatory landscape for diagnostics in India remains fragmented, with varying levels of adoption and enforcement across states. This lack of uniformity can increase compliance complexity for multi-location operators and may impact standardisation of service quality across regions.
Presence of Unorganised and Unregulated 
Laboratories
A significant portion of the diagnostics market continues 
to be served by unorganised players, including laboratories operating without standardised accreditation or quality controls. This may affect overall service reliability and pricing dynamics within the industry, while also posing challenges to organised players focussed on maintaining high quality and compliance standards.

FY 2025-26 Performance Review 
FY 2025-26 was a year of disciplined execution and broad-
based growth, as the Company successfully translated its strategic priorities into strong financial and operational performance. At the MHL Group level*, revenue from operations increased by 24% to ` 1,646 crore, while EBITDA 
grew by 32% to `401 crore, with EBITDA margin improving to 24.4%. Profit After Tax (PAT) increased by 31% to `191 crore, reflecting improved operating leverage, disciplined cost management and the successful integration of acquired businesses. The previous year’s reported EBITDA and PAT included one-time expenses of approximately `21 crore, primarily relating to acquisition-related costs, legal and professional fees associated with ongoing tax matters, and a minor inventory provision.
The Company’s performance was underpinned by 
sustained demand across both consumer and institutional segments, supported by healthy patient volume growth, an improved test mix and continued momentum in specialised diagnostics. On an MHL Organic basis, patient volumes increased by 7.5% to 13.5 million, while test volumes grew by 8.0% to 28.4 million.* Revenue per patient improved by 6%, reflecting a higher contribution from specialty diagnostics and preventive healthcare offerings. Organic B2C revenue grew by 14%, while B2B revenue increased by 13% in FY26. TruHealth and Specialty Diagnostics Management Discussion and Analysis (Contd.)
recorded growth of 21% and 16%, respectively for organic business, reinforcing the Company’s strategy of driving premiumisation and enhancing revenue quality.
Operationally, the Company further strengthened its 
long-term growth platform through strategic acquisitions, network expansion and technology-led transformation. During the year, Metropolis successfully integrated Dr Ahujas’ Pathology and Imaging Centre (DAPIC) in Dehradun,  Scientific Pathology in Agra and Ambika Pathology in Kolhapur into its operating platform, while progressing the integration of Core Diagnostics. The Company expanded its footprint by adding approximately 490 service centres, taking its network to 5,026 service touchpoints across more than 750 towns, thereby strengthening its presence in high-growth markets and improving access to quality diagnostics. Investments in digital capabilities, automation, scientific innovation and operational excellence further enhanced customer experience, productivity and scalability, reinforcing the Company’s differentiated, technology-enabled and science-led operating model.

STRATEGIC ACQUISITIONS AND INTEGRATION
During FY 2025-26, the Company completed three 
strategic acquisitions that strengthened its presence in high-growth regional markets. DAPIC Metropolis Healthcare Private Limited (formerly known as Metropolis Histoxpert Digital Services Private Limited), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Metropolis Healthcare Limited, acquired the entire business of Dr. Alok Ahuja and Dr. Alka Ahuja and Dr. Ahujas' Pathology & Imaging Centre (DAPIC), a partnership firm of Dr. Alok Ahuja and Dr. Alka Ahuja, as a going concern, effective May 23, 2025.
Further, Scientific Metropolis Pathology Private Limited 
(formerly known as Metropolis Clinical Pathology Private Limited), a subsidiary of Metropolis Healthcare Limited, acquired the entire business of Dr. Ashok Kumar Sharma's Scientific Pathology, a sole proprietorship firm of Dr. Ashok Kumar Sharma, as a going concern, effective June 16, 2025.
The Company also acquired the entire business of Dr. RS 
Patil's Ambika Pathology Laboratory, a sole proprietorship firm of Dr. Rajendra Sadashiv Patil, comprising pathology laboratories in Kolhapur, Maharashtra, as a going concern, with effect from September 18, 2025.
From Acquisition to Integration — and Next, AccelerationFY 2025-26 marked a year in which the Company 
demonstrated its ability to integrate acquired businesses effectively. The Company follows a structured integration playbook: the first year focusses on integration and synergy capture, the second on revenue acceleration, and the third on convergence towards company-level margins. Guided by a dedicated steering committee, the Company integrated four acquisitions – Core Diagnostics, Scientific Pathology, DAPIC, and Ambika Pathology-into its operating platform by merging overlapping laboratories, consolidating procurement, standardising operating procedures, and aligning teams around a common performance architecture.
The benefits of this disciplined approach are already 
evident. Core Diagnostics exited the year with high single-digit EBITDA margins and has emerged as a strategic platform for the Company's oncology and genomics businesses. Scientific Pathology and DAPIC delivered growth in line with the Company while operating at margins above the Company average. In Kolhapur, the integration of Ambika Pathology strengthened the Company's regional leadership by creating the largest laboratory in the market. Together, the acquired businesses contributed approximately 8% of Group revenue and increased North India's share of the Company's business from 8% to 17%.With the first phase of integration complete, FY 2026-27 will mark the beginning of the second phase-accelerating growth by cross-selling specialised test menus across acquired channels, deepening clinician engagement, and widening access to specialised diagnostics, supported by an integration framework that the Company has now institutionalised for future opportunities.
RESTRUCTURING
During the year, the Company on February 04, 2026, entered into a Business Transfer Agreement to transfer its External Quality Assessment Services (EQAS) business to its wholly-owned subsidiary, Metropolis Quality Solutions Private Limited (MQSPL), on a going concern basis. The transfer is intended to enable the EQAS business to operate as a separate and independent unit, focussing on its core services, with dedicated management and resources to drive efficiency, excellence, and growth potential. The transfer consideration is up to `1.25 crore, 
subject to closing adjustments, and is proposed to be discharged through cash and/or issuance of equity shares by MQSPL.

QUALITY AND SCIENTIFIC EXCELLENCE
Quality and scientific excellence remain the cornerstone of Metropolis Healthcare Limited's ("the Company") competitive differentiation and long-term growth strategy. The Company has embedded quality across every stage of the diagnostic value chain through its enterprise-wide Quality Intelligence Framework, which integrates governance, digital quality analytics, standardised laboratory practices, accreditation, scientific oversight and a culture of continuous improvement. This integrated framework strengthens diagnostic accuracy, operational consistency and regulatory compliance, while reinforcing trust among patients, clinicians and institutional partners.
During FY 2025-26, the Company maintained 99.9% 
report accuracy and achieved 100% compliance with ISO 15189:2022 across its accredited laboratories, while continuing to strengthen quality governance through its proprietary Quality Index and technology-enabled quality monitoring systems. 
Scientific innovation continued to strengthen the 
Company's leadership in specialised diagnostics. During the year, Metropolis strengthened its portfolio by adding 345 diagnostic tests through new launches and the integration of the Core Diagnostics portfolio. These included 224 next generation sequencing (NGS) tests and 50 precision oncology assays, further supporting growth in genomics. The Company further strengthened its Centre of Genomics through two CAP-accredited laboratories, the commissioning of the Illumina’s NovaSeq™ X Series and collaborations with leading academic institutions, enhancing its capabilities in precision diagnostics and advanced molecular testing. During the year, Metropolis also became the first listed diagnostics company in India to receive a patent in tuberculosis diagnostics, reinforcing its commitment to scientific innovation, indigenous research and differentiated diagnostic capabilities.
The Company continues to strengthen scientific leadership 
through research, medical education and capability development, while investing in the next-generation of healthcare professionals through the Metropolis Institute of Laboratory Education & Skilling (MiLES). These initiatives reinforce the Company's position as a trusted, science-led diagnostics organisation and support its long-term strategy of delivering differentiated, high-quality diagnostic services.

Key Risks and Mitigation Strategies 
Risk Impact Mitigation Plan
Competition RiskThe Company operates in an intensely 
competitive environment influenced by both global and domestic players. Emerging competitors and evolving business models may increase pricing pressure and influence market share. Although the diagnostics industry benefits from growing demand and long-term expansion potential, heightened competition may affect pricing power and margins, which could impact profitability and returns.To mitigate the impact of increasing competition, the Company continues to strengthen its competitive position through scientific differentiation, expansion of specialised diagnostics, superior customer experience and sustained investments in digital capabilities. It remains focussed on cost optimisation, operational excellence and productivity enhancement to strengthen margins, improve return ratios and drive sustainable growth. 
Simultaneously, the Company continues to expand its 
laboratory network and customer touchpoints, improving accessibility, deepening market penetration and supporting volume-led growth. The Company’s core business, particularly acute illness diagnostics, remains relatively resilient to competitive disruption, providing stability in a dynamic market environment. In addition, a dedicated Competition Desk continuously monitors market dynamics, pricing trends, competitive benchmarks and emerging business models, enabling timely strategic interventions and reinforcing the Company’s competitive positioning.
Technology & Innovation RiskIn a rapidly evolving technological landscape, the Company faces the risk that emerging technologies and continuous innovation could render existing systems, platforms or services less competitive. The increasing adoption of automation, artificial intelligence (AI), digital platforms and advanced diagnostics is reshaping the industry, requiring continuous investments in technology upgrades, innovation and capability enhancement to maintain operational efficiency, service excellence and long-term competitiveness.To address this risk, Metropolis continues to invest in advanced technologies, laboratory automation, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital platforms to enhance diagnostic accuracy, operational efficiency and customer experience. The Company is strengthening its technology ecosystem through laboratory platform standardisation, intelligent workflow automation, AI-enabled diagnostic solutions and enterprise-wide digital transformation initiatives. Continuous investments in modern laboratory infrastructure, scientific innovation and employee capability development ensure the organisation remains agile, technologically relevant and well positioned to respond to evolving industry requirements.
IT Disruptions and System Failure RiskGiven the Company’s extensive reliance on technology and data systems, any malfunction, cyberattack, or operational disruption could negatively impact business continuity and service delivery. Failure to maintain robust information security and governance frameworks may expose the Company to risks such as data breaches, operational interruptions, and reputational damage.Metropolis has established a robust information security and cybersecurity framework, supported by ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certifications, reflecting its commitment to globally recognised standards for information security and privacy management. 
The Company continuously strengthens its cyber resilience 
through secure IT architecture, governance frameworks, regular vulnerability assessments, penetration testing and independent third-party audits. Continuous monitoring, preventive controls and periodic disaster recovery testing further enhance business continuity, safeguard patient data and ensure uninterrupted operations.
Business Continuity RiskBusiness operations may be disrupted by external events such as natural disasters, public health emergencies, civil disturbances, geopolitical developments or supply chain interruptions. Such events could impact laboratory operations, logistics, service delivery and the Company's ability to provide uninterrupted diagnostic services.Metropolis has established a comprehensive Business Continuity Planning (BCP) and Disaster Recovery (DR) framework across its Global Reference Laboratory (GRL) and Regional Reference Laboratories (RRLs). Dedicated BCP and DR sites, supported by defined response protocols, periodic testing and continuous monitoring, help ensure operational resilience, minimise service disruptions and maintain uninterrupted diagnostic services during unforeseen events.Management Discussion and Analysis (Contd.)

facilities, external quality assurance programmes, internal audits and structured governance reviews, the framework enables proactive identification of quality risks, timely corrective actions and continuous improvement. INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM
Metropolis Healthcare has instituted a robust internal 
control framework that governs both financial and operational functions across the organisation. These controls are supported by well-documented policies and standard operating procedures designed to ensure accurate financial reporting, operational integrity, regulatory compliance, and asset protection. 
The internal control system provides reasonable 
assurance regarding the reliability of financial and operational information, safeguarding of assets against unauthorised use or losses, and adherence to applicable laws and regulations. Regular reviews are conducted to assess and enhance the effectiveness of these controls. 
The internal audit function, with a clearly-defined 
scope and coverage, plays a critical role in evaluating and strengthening the control environment. Key focus areas include:
•
 Identifying and reporting key process risks
• Ve
rifying compliance with statutory requirements and 
internal guidelines 
• Re

efficiency and operational effectiveness
• Ensuring the accuracy and dependability of financial 
and operational data.

udit Committee of the Board provides active

COMPANY OUTLOOK
The long-term outlook for the Indian diagnostics industry remains favourable, supported by rising healthcare awareness, increasing adoption of preventive healthcare, growing demand for specialised diagnostics and genomics, expanding health insurance coverage and the continued shift towards organised, quality-led diagnostic providers. These structural trends are expected to create significant long-term opportunities for established players with strong scientific capabilities, trusted brands and scalable operating models.
Building on the strong foundations established over 
the past few years, Metropolis Healthcare Limited (“the Company”) is well positioned to capture these opportunities through its differentiated scientific expertise, technology-enabled operating model, expanding network and customer-centric approach. Going forward, the Company will remain focussed on driving sustainable growth through productivity enhancement, operational excellence, specialty diagnostics, digital transformation and disciplined capital allocation, while continuing to strengthen its market leadership.
Supported by a strong balance sheet, robust governance 
framework and a disciplined execution strategy, the Company remains confident of delivering sustainable, profitable growth and creating long-term value for patients, clinicians, shareholders and all other stakeholders.

1 Energy 
ManagementOpportunity The Company 
operates energy-intensive diagnostic laboratories and infrastructure, making energy consumption a significant operational and environmental consideration. Metropolis is focused on improving energy efficiency through optimization of operations, adoption of energy-efficient equipment, and integration of sustainable practices across facilities. Continuous monitoring of energy usage is undertaken to identify opportunities for reduction.Positive Impact: Improved energy efficiency can lead to cost savings, reduced operational expenses, and a lower environmental footprint, contributing to long-term sustainability.
2 Waste 
ManagementRisk Biomedical waste is an 
inherent by-product of diagnostic services and laboratory operations, requiring strict handling and disposal protocols to mitigate environmental and health risks.Biomedical waste is handled in compliance with regulatory standards through a government-authorized partner. It is systematically segregated using color-coded bags and barcodes, weighed for tracking, and managed with strict safety protocols from the point of generation to final disposalNegative Impact: Improper waste disposal could result in regulatory penalties, reputational damage, health hazards, and potential disruption of operations, including risks to licensing and compliance status.
3 Employee Health 
and SafetyRisk Inadequate safety 
measures can lead to increased instances of employee injuries and health-related issues, resulting in higher absenteeism and reduced operational efficiency. Additionally, lapses in workplace safety may negatively impact employee morale and trust in the organization, ultimately affecting productivity and job satisfaction. Therefore, prioritizing employee health and safety is critical to sustaining a motivated, engaged, and high-performing workforce.Employee well-being, health, and safety remain core priorities for the Company. Laboratory facilities and infrastructure are designed in accordance with prescribed safety standards, with clear segregation between administrative and laboratory areas to minimize risk exposure. The Company conducts regular fire and electrical safety inspections and has established comprehensive policies and procedures to proactively identify and mitigate potential hazards. These risk assessment protocols are formally documented in the safety manual and are supported by periodic safety audits conducted by the Quality Assurance team to ensure continuous compliance and adherence to best practices.Negative Impact: Workplace incidents may lead to increased healthcare costs, employee attrition, reduced productivity, legal liabilities, and operational inefficiencies.

5. Specific commitments, goals and targets set b
y the 
entity with defined timelines, if any.Metropolis Healthcare has established a comprehensive set of ESG 
commitments with defined medium- and long-term targets to create sustainable value for all stakeholders. 
The Company aims to achieve a 45% reduction in greenhouse gas 
emissions intensity and source ~ 50% of its electricity from renewable energy by FY2030, while progressing towards Net Zero emissions by FY2043. It is also committed to reducing plastic usage by 50% by FY2030, lowering water intensity by 30% by FY2043, and working towards Zero Waste to Landfill by FY2030. On the social front, the Company aspires to achieve a 50:50 gender-balanced workforce by FY2028, maintain a Net Promoter Score (NPS) above 90, and positively impact one million lives through its community health initiatives by FY2043. 
These commitments are supported by a strong governance framework 
focused on maintaining the highest standards of ethics, regulatory compliance, information security, and data privacy. Progress against these targets is reviewed periodically through established governance mechanisms, ensuring accountability and continuous improvement in the Company's ESG performance.
6.
 Perf
ormance of the entity against the specific 
commitments, goals and targets along-with reasons in case the same are not met.During FY2025–26, Metropolis Healthcare continued to make measurable progress against its ESG commitments across environmental stewardship, social responsibility and governance. The Company strengthened its environmental performance by sourcing approximately 30% of the electricity consumed at the Metropolis Global Reference Laboratory from renewable energy, initiating a 100kW rooftop solar programme across select facilities, and improving energy efficiency through infrastructure upgrades, including LED lighting, HVAC optimisation and laboratory process enhancements. Focused initiatives in waste management and water conservation further supported responsible resource utilisation and operational sustainability.
On the social front, the Company maintained a Net Promoter Score 
(NPS) of 87, reflecting its continued focus on customer satisfaction and service excellence. The Company also strengthened its commitment to diversity and inclusion, with women constituting ~ 44% of the overall workforce. 
From a governance perspective, Metropolis continued to uphold robust 
standards of ethical business conduct, information security and data privacy by maintaining ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certifications. Progress against ESG commitments is periodically reviewed through established governance mechanisms to ensure effective oversight and continuous improvement. 
The Company's long-term ESG commitments, including increasing

7. Stat
ement by director responsible for the business 
responsibility report, highlighting ESG related 
challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure) At Metropolis Healthcare, sustainability is integral to our purpose of enabling healthier lives and creating long-term value for all stakeholders. As healthcare continues to evolve, we recognise that delivering high-quality diagnostics must go hand in hand with responsible environmental stewardship, inclusive growth and strong governance. ESG is therefore embedded into our business strategy, guiding decisions across our operations, people, innovation and community initiatives.
During FY2025–26, we continued to strengthen our sustainability 
performance through focused investments in energy efficiency, renewable energy adoption, responsible waste management and water conservation. We also advanced our digital transformation initiatives to enhance operational efficiency while reducing resource consumption. Across our social agenda, we remained committed to expanding access to quality healthcare, strengthening customer trust, fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace, and investing in employee capability and well-being. Our community programmes continued to create measurable social impact by advancing adolescent health, preventive healthcare and medical education, in alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
While we have made meaningful progress, we recognise that the 
transition towards a more sustainable future requires continuous effort and collaboration. Increasing climate resilience across our operations, accelerating renewable energy adoption, strengthening resource efficiency and embedding sustainability across our expanding network remain key priorities as we progress towards our long-term ESG commitments.
Strong governance remains the cornerstone of our sustainability 
journey. Through robust risk management, ethical business practices, information security, regulatory compliance and transparent stakeholder engagement, we continue to reinforce trust and accountability across our business.
Looking ahead, we remain committed to integrating sustainability into 
every aspect of our organisation. By combining scientific excellence, innovation and responsible business practices, we will continue to create sustainable value for our patients, employees, partners, investors and communities while contributing meaningfully to a healthier and more sustainable future.

EI-10. a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the 
entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the coverage such system?
Yes. The Company has implemented an Occupational Health and Safety Management System covering its employees, 
operations and facilities. The system is aligned with applicable health, safety and biomedical waste management regulations, ISO 15189 requirements, and internal policies. Metropolis continues to monitor occupational health and safety performance through established incident reporting, risk assessment and corrective action mechanisms to promote a safe and healthy workplace.
EI-10. b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and 
non-routine basis by the entity?
The Company has established processes to identify, assess and manage work-related hazards across its operations. 
Routine risk assessments are carried out through safety inspections, compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs), equipment maintenance, monitoring of personal protective equipment (PPE) usage, and adherence to biosafety and biomedical waste management protocols. Non-routine risks are evaluated during the introduction of new equipment, process modifications and incident investigations through structured risk assessments, root cause analysis, safety audits, mock drills and periodic employee training, enabling timely implementation of preventive and corrective actions. 
EI-10. c. Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove 
themselves from such risks. (Y/N)
Yes. The Company has established processes for employees and workers to report work-related hazards and unsafe 
conditions through their reporting managers, Lab Heads, the Human Resources function or designated safety personnel. Employees are encouraged to report concerns promptly and may remove themselves from situations that pose an imminent risk to their health or safety until appropriate corrective measures are implemented.
EI-10.d. Do the employees/ worker of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare 
services? (Yes/ No)
All the employees have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services. They are covered either under a 
Group Mediclaim Policy or through ESIC, depending on eligibility and applicability.

 PRINCIPLE 4
Businesses should respect the interests of and be responsive to all its stakeholders
 Essential Indicators
EI-1. Describe the processes for identifying key stakeholder groups of the entity.
Metropolis Healthcare adopts a structured and ongoing approach to identify and prioritise stakeholders who are impacted 
by, or have the ability to influence, the Company’s business, strategy and sustainability performance. Stakeholder groups are identified based on their relationship with the Company, the significance of their influence, the extent of the Company’s impact on them, and their relevance to long-term value creation. 
The Company’s key stakeholders include patients, employees, clinicians, investors, suppliers, regulators, business 
partners, communities and other relevant stakeholders. Their perspectives are captured through regular engagement mechanisms such as surveys, consultations, feedback platforms, grievance redressal channels, governance forums and collaborative partnerships.
Insights from these engagements are integrated into the Company’s risk management, materiality assessment and 
strategic decision-making processes, enabling Metropolis to address stakeholder expectations, strengthen responsible business practices and advance its sustainability priorities. The stakeholder identification process is reviewed periodically to reflect the evolving business environment, emerging ESG issues and changing stakeholder expectationsBusiness Responsibility and Sustainability Report (Contd.)

LI-1. Provide the processes for consultation between stakeholders and the Board on economic, environmental, and social topics or if consultation is delegated, how is feedback from such consultations provided to the Board.
Stakeholder engagement on economic, environmental and social matters is primarily undertaken by the respective 
business functions through established engagement channels. Material stakeholder concerns, emerging ESG risks and key opportunities are consolidated by the management and reviewed by the Company’s Key Managerial Personnel (KMP).
